Edges offered: | edge | |---| | err:if_statement->BracelessMultiStatementBody | wrong rule: Indenting several statements under an if or for makes them all part of its body, even without braces. | right rule: Without braces only the first statement belongs to the if/for; the rest run once, after it. | | err:if_statement->CurlyIfCondition | wrong rule: Writes the if condition inside { } instead of ( ). | right rule: The condition of an if is written in parentheses. | | err:if_statement->SemicolonAfterIfHeader | wrong rule: if (x > 0); System.out.println("positive"); prints only for positive x. | right rule: The ; ends the if with an empty statement, so the next line always runs. | | mis:if_statement->AssignCompares | wrong rule: = compares two values instead of assigning | right rule: x = y copies the value of y into x; x == y is what compares them. | | mis:if_statement->BranchChosenByIntent | wrong rule: Which branch runs is decided by what the programmer meant or by code outside the if, not by whether the condition is true. | right rule: The then branch runs exactly when the condition evaluates to true at the moment it is tested; otherwise the else branch (if any) runs. | | mis:if_statement->CodeAfterIfSkipped | wrong rule: When the then branch runs, the code after the if is skipped. | right rule: After the if finishes, execution continues with the next statement either way. | | mis:if_statement->FalseConditionEndsProgram | wrong rule: A false condition with no else ends the program. | right rule: When an if condition is false and there is no else, execution continues with the statement after the if. | | mis:if_statement->FalseConditionRestartsProgram | wrong rule: When an if condition is false (and there is no else), control jumps back to the start of the program. | right rule: A false condition skips the then branch and execution continues with the statement after the if statement. | | mis:if_statement->IfConditionCheckedInHindsight | wrong rule: Whether the branch runs is decided by the condition after the branch, or from the point inside the body where the condition becomes true. | right rule: The condition is tested once, before the branch; the whole branch runs if it was true at that moment and none of it runs otherwise. | | mis:if_statement->IfConditionWatched | wrong rule: An if statement watches its condition while the program runs and fires as soon as the condition becomes true (if = whenever). | right rule: An if condition is tested once, when control reaches the if statement; later changes to the variables do not trigger the branch. | | mis:if_statement->IfInLoopUnchecked | wrong rule: An if inside a loop body runs its branch on every pass without testing its condition. | right rule: The if condition is tested again on every pass, with the current values, so the branch runs only on passes where it is true. | | mis:if_statement->IfIsLoop | wrong rule: The if body keeps repeating as long as its condition stays true. | right rule: An if body runs at most once; only a loop repeats its body. | | mis:if_statement->IfRequiresElse | wrong rule: Every if statement requires an else. | right rule: An if statement may stand alone; the else part is optional. | | mis:if_statement->IfWaitsForCondition | wrong rule: An IF statement earlier in the program stays active and fires later, e.g. inside a later loop, when its condition becomes true. | right rule: An if is evaluated once when control reaches it; afterwards it is inactive unless control returns to it. | | mis:if_statement->LoopForOneTimeTest | wrong rule: Uses a loop where a condition needs to be tested only once. | right rule: A test made once is an if; a loop repeats. | | mis:if_statement->MapToBooleanWithIf | wrong rule: you need an if to turn a boolean expression into a boolean | right rule: ok = (x > y); stores the result of the comparison directly. | | mis:if_statement->MissingBraces | wrong rule: Omits braces around a single-statement body of if, for or while. | right rule: Braces are optional for a single-statement body, but using them anyway avoids bugs when statements are added later. | | mis:if_statement->NextStatementIsElse | wrong rule: In if (c) A; B; the statement B runs only when c is false. | right rule: B is not part of the if; it runs every time. | | mis:if_statement->ProgramLooksAhead | wrong rule: The program knows or sees what later lines will do and acts on those goals at the current line, e.g. it stops 'at ten' because it wants to draw a box. | right rule: Each statement executes using only the current state; later lines have no effect until control reaches them. | | mis:if_statement->SequentialIfsAreNested | wrong rule: Of two if statements one after the other, the second runs its body only if both conditions are true. | right rule: Two ifs in sequence are independent: each tests only its own condition. | | mis:if_statement->StatementAfterIfInBranch | wrong rule: A statement placed after the if statement belongs to its branch, so it runs only when the condition is true. | right rule: The branch ends at its closing brace (or after its single statement);
